questions.prompt: The previous level named Torah, prophets, and wisdom as real Old Testament genres. Why does actually knowing a passage's own real genre matter for reading it well?
choices: A real genre sets legitimate expectations for how a passage communicates truth -- reading it as the wrong genre distorts it
Because genre has no real, practical bearing on how a passage should actually be read
Because every real genre in Scripture actually communicates truth in exactly the identical real way
Because knowing a passage's own real genre actually makes careful reading unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: A real genre sets legitimate expectations for how a passage communicates truth -- reading it as the wrong genre distorts it
questions.explanation: Genre sets real, legitimate expectations for how a passage actually communicates truth -- a real poem (like many Psalms) works differently than a real legal text (like Leviticus), and reading either as the wrong real genre distorts what it actually says.
questions.hint: Consider what would happen if a real poem were read as if it were a real, literal legal code, or the reverse.

questions.prompt: True or False: Reading the Book of Job's own real poetic dialogue as if it were a precise, literal historical transcript would actually distort what the book is genuinely trying to communicate.
questions.explanation: True. Job's own real, poetic dialogue wrestles with the real question of innocent suffering through a real literary form -- reading it as a precise historical transcript would actually miss what that real literary form is doing.
questions.hint: Recall the previous level's own real teaching on wisdom literature and its own real, characteristic literary form.

questions.prompt: This level's own real point -- genre sets real, legitimate reading expectations -- connects directly to this topic's earlier level on inerrancy. How?

Because genre and inerrancy actually have no real connection to one another
Because this level's own real point actually contradicts the earlier level's own real teaching on inerrancy
Because inerrancy makes genre analysis entirely unnecessary

questions.explanation: This is a real, direct fulfillment of a promise this topic's own earlier level made -- genre discernment is precisely the real skill needed to tell incidental, ancient detail apart from Scripture's own real, saving truth.
questions.hint: Recall this topic's own earlier level on inerrancy, and what real, further skill it said would be needed to actually discern saving truth from incidental detail.

questions.hint: Consider what real genre the Ten Commandments themselves are actually given in, and what that genre would lead a reader to expect.

questions.explanation: This objection assumes genre is chosen conveniently after the fact. In fact, real genre is determined through real, careful, honest literary and historical analysis -- the Ten Commandments' own real, legal genre is not remotely ambiguous, exactly the kind of real, honest discipline this topic's own earlier levels have already modeled.

questions.prompt: The first three Gospels -- Matthew, Mark, and Luke -- are called the 'Synoptic Gospels' because they:
choices: Share a similar structure, content, and viewpoint, and so can be 'seen together'
Were all written by the same single author
Are the only Gospels considered inspired
Were written after the Gospel of John
questions.correctAnswer: Share a similar structure, content, and viewpoint, and so can be 'seen together'
questions.explanation: 'Synoptic' comes from Greek meaning 'seen together' -- these three Gospels share substantial overlapping material and can be usefully compared side by side, unlike John's distinct approach.
questions.hint: 'Syn-optic' literally means 'together-view.'

citations.quote: the four Gospels... faithfully hand on what Jesus, the Son of God, while he lived among men, really did and taught for their eternal salvation.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Gospel of John is typically grouped together with Matthew, Mark, and Luke as one of the 'Synoptic Gospels.'
questions.explanation: John stands apart from the other three, with a distinct structure, style, and theological emphasis -- it is not counted among the Synoptics.
questions.hint: This is the one Gospel that stands apart from the other three, stylistically.

citations.quote: the four Gospels... faithfully hand on what Jesus, the Son of God, while he lived among men, really did and taught for their eternal salvation.

questions.prompt: The Catechism describes the Gospels as the 'heart of all the Scriptures' because they are our principal source for the life and ____ of the Incarnate Word.
questions.explanation: Everything else in Scripture -- Old and New Testament alike -- is read in relation to the Gospels, since they record Christ's own words and deeds most directly.
questions.hint: Alongside 'life,' this word is what the Gospels record about Christ's own words.

citations.quote: The Gospels are the heart of all the Scriptures 'because they are our principal source for the life and teaching of the Incarnate Word, our Saviour.'

questions.prompt: The Catechism describes the formation of the Gospels happening in three stages: the life and teaching of Jesus, the oral Tradition of the apostles, and finally:
choices: The Gospels being written down by the four evangelists
The Gospels being translated into Latin
The Council of Trent formally approving them
The invention of the printing press
questions.correctAnswer: The Gospels being written down by the four evangelists
questions.explanation: The evangelists, drawing on the earlier oral preaching of the apostolic Church, put this apostolic testimony into writing, 'selecting' and 'synthesizing' it for their particular communities.
questions.hint: This is the final stage, after Jesus' own ministry and the apostles' preaching about it.

citations.quote: the four Gospels... faithfully hand on what Jesus, the Son of God, while he lived among men, really did and taught for their eternal salvation.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Church requires every one of the four evangelists to have personally witnessed the entirety of Jesus' earthly ministry firsthand.
questions.explanation: The Gospels' reliability rests on their rootedness in apostolic testimony passed down faithfully, not on a requirement that every individual evangelist personally witnessed every event they recorded.
questions.hint: What matters is the Gospels' connection to apostolic testimony as a whole, not each author's personal presence at every event.

citations.quote: the four Gospels... faithfully hand on what Jesus, the Son of God, while he lived among men, really did and taught for their eternal salvation.

questions.prompt: Match each Gospel to a distinguishing note about it.

pairs.right: Written with a strongly Jewish audience and Old Testament fulfillment in mind
Shortest Gospel, fast-paced, emphasizing Christ's suffering servanthood
Emphasizes mercy, the poor, and salvation's universal reach
Distinct in style, emphasizing Christ's divinity and 'I am' statements

questions.explanation: Each evangelist writes with his own emphasis and audience in mind, while all four together present one coherent portrait of Christ.
questions.hint: One is Jewish-focused, one is fast and Passion-focused, one favors the poor, one is theologically distinct.

citations.quote: The Gospels are the heart of all the Scriptures 'because they are our principal source for the life and teaching of the Incarnate Word, our Saviour.'

questions.prompt: What distinguishes the Gospel of John most sharply from the Synoptic Gospels in its portrait of Jesus?
choices: John emphasizes lengthy discourses and explicit statements of Jesus's divine identity ('I am' sayings), where the Synoptics favor parables and shorter sayings
John omits the crucifixion entirely
John is the only Gospel written by a non-eyewitness
John contains no miracles, unlike the Synoptics
questions.correctAnswer: John emphasizes lengthy discourses and explicit statements of Jesus's divine identity ('I am' sayings), where the Synoptics favor parables and shorter sayings
questions.explanation: John's high Christology is stated openly and often (I am the bread of life, the light of the world, the good shepherd), where the Synoptics let Jesus's identity emerge more gradually through action and parable — a real difference in approach, not a contradiction between them.
questions.hint: Compare how directly each Gospel has Jesus state who he is.

questions.prompt: True or False: The Catechism describes the Gospels as arising in three identifiable stages: the life and teaching of Jesus, the apostolic preaching, and the written composition by the evangelists.
questions.explanation: True, and this three-stage account is the Church's own careful answer to how eyewitness memory, oral proclamation, and finally written text relate to each other — it neither treats the Gospels as raw transcripts nor as late inventions disconnected from the events.
questions.hint: The three stages move from an event, through preaching, to a written text.

questions.prompt: The Catechism calls the Gospels the '____ of all the Scriptures,' because they are our principal source for Christ's life and teaching.
questions.explanation: Calling the Gospels the heart of Scripture does not diminish the rest of the Bible; it names their central place, since everything else in Scripture is read in relation to the Christ the Gospels present directly.
questions.hint: The metaphor names the Gospels' central place among all of Scripture's books.

questions.prompt: Match each Gospel to a distinguishing note about it.

pairs.right: Written with a strong eye to Jesus fulfilling Old Testament prophecy
The shortest Gospel, likely the earliest written
Paired with Acts, with particular attention to the marginalized
High Christology, extended discourses, and 'I am' sayings

questions.explanation: Each evangelist writes with a real theological emphasis and a particular audience in mind, without contradicting the others — four true, complementary portraits of one Christ, not four competing or inconsistent accounts.
questions.hint: Each has one especially recognizable feature: brevity, fulfillment, companionship with a second book, or explicit theology.

questions.prompt: The previous level covered all four Gospels. A skeptic asks: 'If they're all about the same Jesus, why does the Church need four Gospels instead of just one complete, unified account?' What is the real, careful answer?
choices: Each Gospel offers a distinct, complementary portrait of Christ, giving a fuller picture than any one account alone
The Church actually has no real, coherent answer to this specific real question
The four Gospels actually tell four entirely separate, unrelated real stories about four different people
Having four Gospels was purely accidental, with no real theological reasoning behind keeping all four
questions.correctAnswer: Each Gospel offers a distinct, complementary portrait of Christ, giving a fuller picture than any one account alone
questions.explanation: Four real, distinct, complementary portraits of the very same Christ -- each shaped by its own real author and audience -- together give a richer, fuller real picture than any single account could alone, not four competing or contradictory versions.
questions.hint: Consider what four real, different portraits of the very same person could actually offer, compared to only one.

questions.prompt: A skeptic pushes further: 'Couldn't the Church have picked the single best Gospel and set the other three aside?' What is the real, careful answer?

Yes -- the objection is correct, and the Church really should have kept only a single Gospel
No -- because the four Gospels are actually word-for-word identical, making the question meaningless

questions.correctAnswer: No -- each Gospel adds real content the others don't; setting one aside would lose content, not trim redundancy
questions.explanation: This objection assumes the four Gospels are redundant, so one could stand in for the rest. In fact, each Gospel's own real, distinct portrait genuinely adds something real the others do not -- setting any aside would lose real, genuine content, not merely trim redundancy.
questions.hint: Consider whether the four Gospels' own real differences are actually redundant repetition, or genuine, distinct real content.
